project.name: unihack8
project.description: Hackathon mobile app for Timișoara (Connected Communities): events with QR check-in and reliability points, a filterable map of places, live STPT public transport, directions, and an AI guide. Spring Boot backend + Supabase Postgres; Expo frontend.

nodes.name: PageParams.java
nodes.summary: Immutable paging-parameter record enforcing the API paging rules (page from 0, default size 20, max 100 for lists and 500 for map bbox queries) and converting them to a Spring Data Pageable.

nodes.name: PageParams
nodes.summary: Java record holding validated page/size values with static factories of() and forMap() that throw VALIDATION_FAILED ApiExceptions on out-of-range input, plus toPageable(Sort).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a Java record with static factory methods and a private overloaded validator.

nodes.name: of
nodes.summary: Shared validator that defaults null page/size, checks page >= 0 and 1 <= size <= maxSize, and throws ApiException(VALIDATION_FAILED) otherwise; public of(page,size) and forMap delegate to it.

nodes.name: ApiException.java
nodes.summary: Custom runtime exception carrying an ErrorCode and message, used throughout the backend to signal business and validation errors that the global handler turns into JSON error responses.

nodes.name: ApiException
nodes.summary: RuntimeException subclass wrapping an ErrorCode with optional custom message, offering a notFound() convenience factory and a code() accessor.

nodes.name: ErrorCode.java
nodes.summary: Enum catalogue of every API error code (validation, auth, event participation, QR check-in, rate limiting, internal) mapped to its HTTP status and default user-facing message.

nodes.name: ErrorCode
nodes.summary: Enum whose constants pair an HttpStatus with a default message, e.g. EVENT_FULL (409), TICKET_NOT_FOUND (404), UNAUTHORIZED (401), exposed via status() and defaultMessage().
nodes.languageNotes: Java enum with constructor-backed fields acting as a typed error registry.

nodes.name: CurrentUser.java
nodes.summary: Spring component that resolves the calling user's UUID from the Supabase JWT 'sub' claim in the security context, for use by controllers and services.

nodes.name: CurrentUser
nodes.summary: @Component exposing id(), which throws UNAUTHORIZED when no valid token is present, and optionalId(), which returns empty for anonymous or non-UUID subjects.

nodes.name: optionalId
nodes.summary: Reads the Authentication from SecurityContextHolder and, if it is a JwtAuthenticationToken, parses its subject as a UUID; returns Optional.empty() otherwise or on malformed subjects.

nodes.name: PageParamsTest.java
nodes.summary: JUnit tests for PageParams and PageResponse covering defaults, the 100/500 size limits, rejection of negative page and zero size, sort preservation in toPageable, and page-response item mapping.

nodes.name: PageParamsTest
nodes.summary: Unit test class with six cases verifying paging defaults, list and map max sizes, invalid input rejection via ApiException, and Pageable/PageResponse conversion.

nodes.name: CurrentUserTest.java
nodes.summary: JUnit tests for CurrentUser that populate the Spring SecurityContext with JWT tokens to verify subject-to-UUID resolution, anonymous handling, and ignoring of non-UUID subjects.

nodes.name: CurrentUserTest
nodes.summary: Test class with a signInAs helper building JwtAuthenticationTokens and cases asserting id() returns the subject, anonymous callers get UNAUTHORIZED/empty, and bad subjects are ignored.

nodes.name: TestProbeController.java
nodes.summary: Test-only REST controller (lives in src/test, never shipped) exposing probe endpoints to exercise shared security rules, current-user resolution, error handling, body validation and paging before real features exist.

nodes.name: TestProbeController
nodes.summary: @RestController with probe endpoints: public /transit/test-probe, protected /test-probe/me, /full (EVENT_FULL ApiException), /boom (unexpected error), /body (validated ProbeBody record) and /page (PageParams).

nodes.name: ErrorResponse.java
nodes.summary: Immutable record defining the single standard error JSON shape (status, code, message, field errors, timestamp, path) returned by every API endpoint.
nodes.languageNotes: Java record: compact immutable data carrier with auto-generated accessors, equals and hashCode.

nodes.name: ErrorResponse
nodes.summary: Java record holding HTTP status, machine-readable error code, message, optional per-field validation errors, UTC timestamp and request path.

nodes.name: ErrorResponseFactory.java
nodes.summary: Spring component that builds ErrorResponse objects from an ErrorCode, so the controller advice and security handlers produce identical error bodies.

nodes.name: ErrorResponseFactory
nodes.summary: Clock-injected factory with overloaded create methods mapping an ErrorCode plus optional message and field errors into an ErrorResponse, defaulting the message to the code's default.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Overloaded builders that turn an ErrorCode, optional message, optional field map and request path into a timestamped ErrorResponse; empty field maps are normalized to null.

nodes.name: GlobalExceptionHandler.java
nodes.summary: @RestControllerAdvice that converts every controller exception (ApiException, validation failures, unreadable bodies, missing/mistyped params, 404/405, access denied, unexpected errors) into the standard error JSON.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Spring's @ExceptionHandler methods on a @RestControllerAdvice to centralize exception-to-HTTP mapping.

nodes.name: GlobalExceptionHandler
nodes.summary: Central controller advice with one @ExceptionHandler per exception type, each mapping to an ErrorCode and delegating response building to ErrorResponseFactory; unexpected errors are logged without leaking internals.

nodes.name: handleBodyValidation
nodes.summary: Collects field and global errors from a failed @Valid request body into a field map and returns VALIDATION_FAILED.

nodes.name: handleParameterValidation
nodes.summary: Maps @RequestParam/@PathVariable constraint failures from HandlerMethodValidationException into per-parameter field errors.

nodes.name: handleConstraintViolation
nodes.summary: Converts bean-validation ConstraintViolationExceptions raised outside the web layer into field errors keyed by the last property-path segment.

nodes.name: respond
nodes.summary: Private helper building a ResponseEntity with the ErrorCode's HTTP status and a body produced by ErrorResponseFactory.

nodes.name: JsonAccessDeniedHandler.java
nodes.summary: Spring Security AccessDeniedHandler that writes a 403 FORBIDDEN response in the standard error JSON format when an authenticated user lacks permission.

nodes.name: JsonAccessDeniedHandler
nodes.summary: Implements AccessDeniedHandler; sets 403 status and JSON content type, then serializes a FORBIDDEN ErrorResponse via ObjectMapper.

nodes.name: JsonAuthenticationEntryPoint.java
nodes.summary: Spring Security AuthenticationEntryPoint that answers 401 UNAUTHORIZED with the standard error JSON and a WWW-Authenticate: Bearer header when the token is missing, expired or invalid.

nodes.name: JsonAuthenticationEntryPoint
nodes.summary: Implements AuthenticationEntryPoint; sets 401 status, Bearer challenge header and JSON body built from an UNAUTHORIZED ErrorResponse.

nodes.name: SecurityConfig.java
nodes.summary: Spring Security configuration for a stateless JWT resource server: public GET endpoints for events, places and transit, Supabase HS256 token validation with issuer and audience checks, JSON 401/403 handlers and permissive dev CORS.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the Spring Security lambda DSL and a Nimbus JWT decoder with a DelegatingOAuth2TokenValidator to combine default and custom claim checks.

nodes.name: SecurityConfig
nodes.summary: @Configuration class exposing the SecurityFilterChain, JwtDecoder and CorsConfigurationSource beans that secure the API with Supabase access tokens.

nodes.name: securityFilterChain
nodes.summary: Builds the filter chain: disables CSRF, enables CORS, stateless sessions, permits OPTIONS and selected public GET routes, requires authentication elsewhere, and wires the JSON entry point and access-denied handler.

nodes.name: jwtDecoder
nodes.summary: Creates a Nimbus JWT decoder using the legacy Supabase HS256 secret and attaches the issuer/audience validator.

nodes.name: tokenValidator
nodes.summary: Combines default JWT checks (expiry, issuer) with a claim validator requiring the Supabase authenticated audience.

nodes.name: corsConfigurationSource
nodes.summary: Registers an open CORS policy (any origin, common methods and headers) for all paths, intended for Expo web development.

nodes.name: index.jsx
nodes.summary: Expo Router home route (Discover screen) that renders a react-native-maps MapView centered on Timisoara with an overlay card and a 'Locate me' button that requests foreground location permission and animates to the user's position.
nodes.languageNotes: Expo Router file-based routing: the default export of src/app/index.jsx becomes the root '/' screen.

nodes.name: DiscoverScreen
nodes.summary: React component that holds map ref and location state, and defines the locateUser handler which requests permission via expo-location, builds a region with regionForCoordinates, and animates the map to it with user-facing status messages.

nodes.name: api.js
nodes.summary: Minimal HTTP client helpers for the Spring Boot backend: resolves the base URL from EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL and performs JSON GET requests with an injectable fetcher.

nodes.name: apiBaseUrl
nodes.summary: Returns the configured backend base URL (defaulting to EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL) with trailing slashes stripped, throwing if unset.

nodes.name: apiGet
nodes.summary: Performs a JSON GET against the backend by joining the base URL and path, using an optional injected fetcher, and throws an error containing the HTTP status on non-OK responses.

nodes.name: map.js
nodes.summary: Map helpers exporting the frozen TIMISOARA_CENTER coordinates and a validated region builder used by the map screen.

nodes.name: regionForCoordinates
nodes.summary: Builds a react-native-maps region with fixed 0.035 deltas around a point, throwing RangeError for non-finite or out-of-bounds latitude/longitude.

nodes.name: setup.test.mjs
nodes.summary: node:test suite verifying that regionForCoordinates rejects invalid coordinates and that apiBaseUrl/apiGet normalize URLs and surface HTTP status errors using a stubbed fetcher.

nodes.name: GlobalExceptionHandlerTest.java
nodes.summary: Spring Boot MockMvc integration tests verifying that every error (API exceptions, validation failures, malformed JSON, bad params, 404, 405, unexpected 500) is returned in the standard error response shape from docs/API.md.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses @SpringBootTest with @AutoConfigureMockMvc and Hamcrest matchers on jsonPath to assert the JSON error contract.

nodes.name: GlobalExceptionHandlerTest
nodes.summary: Test class with eight MockMvc cases asserting status codes, error codes and the absence of leaked internal details for each error category handled globally.

nodes.name: apiExceptionUsesItsCodeAndStatus
nodes.summary: Checks that a thrown ApiException is rendered with its own error code and HTTP status in the standard error body.

nodes.name: invalidBodyListsFields
nodes.summary: Checks that bean-validation failures on a request body return 400 with the offending field names listed.

nodes.name: SecurityConfigTest.java
nodes.summary: Spring Boot MockMvc integration tests for JWT validation and public/protected route rules, using real HS256 Supabase-style tokens (wrong secret, expired, wrong issuer/audience, malformed, missing).
nodes.languageNotes: Exercises the OAuth2 resource server configuration end to end through a test-only probe controller rather than mocking the security filter chain.

nodes.name: SecurityConfigTest
nodes.summary: Test class with ten cases covering 401 responses for invalid or missing tokens, acceptance of valid tokens with sub as user id, and anonymous access to public endpoints.

nodes.name: protectedEndpointWithoutTokenIs401
nodes.summary: Asserts a protected endpoint without a token returns 401 with a WWW-Authenticate Bearer header and the standard error JSON shape.

nodes.name: JwtTestTokens.java
nodes.summary: Test support utility that signs HS256 JWTs shaped like Supabase access tokens, with defaults matching the test application.properties secret, issuer and audience.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Nimbus JOSE+JWT (MACSigner, JWTClaimsSet) to build signed tokens; final class with private constructor as a static utility.

nodes.name: JwtTestTokens
nodes.summary: Static utility class exposing test secret/issuer/audience constants and helpers to mint valid or deliberately invalid Supabase-style tokens.

nodes.name: valid
nodes.summary: Returns a valid signed token for the given user id that expires in one hour.

nodes.name: sign
nodes.summary: Signs a token with caller-chosen secret, subject, issuer, audience and expiry so tests can construct invalid tokens.

nodes.name: profiles
nodes.summary: Migration creating the public.profiles table (one row per Supabase auth user) with a case-insensitive unique username, trigram search index, a reliability_score defaulting to 100, and row level security enabled.

nodes.name: handle_new_user
nodes.summary: Security-definer PL/pgSQL trigger function that auto-creates a profile for each new auth.users row, using the sign-up metadata username or falling back to a generated user_xxxxxxxx name on invalid or duplicate input.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses security definer with an empty search_path and a nested BEGIN/EXCEPTION block to catch unique_violation, so sign-up never fails; execute is revoked from public roles so only the on_auth_user_created trigger invokes it.

nodes.name: events
nodes.summary: Migration creating public.events for both user-created (USER) and imported (EXTERNAL) events, with location, capacity, pricing in lei, organizer FK to profiles, consistency check constraints, and indexes for date, map-bbox, organizer and fuzzy title queries.

nodes.name: event_participants
nodes.summary: Join table recording which users joined which events, with a status lifecycle (JOINED, ATTENDED, NO_SHOW, CANCELLED, BANNED), a unique QR token for organizer check-in, and a constraint tying ATTENDED status to a check-in timestamp.

nodes.name: reliability_log
nodes.summary: Audit table of signed reliability point changes per user (optionally linked to an event, preserved via ON DELETE SET NULL) that explains the history behind each profile's reliability score.

nodes.name: places
nodes.summary: Migration creating public.places for restaurants, cafes and other POIs imported from OpenStreetMap, keyed by a unique osm_id for upserts, with raw opening_hours, a jsonb tags bag, and category and lat/lon indexes for map filtering.

nodes.name: 20261113000001_profiles.sql
nodes.summary: Migration 1: enables pg_trgm, creates the profiles table and the on_auth_user_created trigger (handle_new_user) that creates a profile on Supabase sign-up.

nodes.name: 20261113000002_events.sql
nodes.summary: Migration 2: creates the events table for USER and EXTERNAL events with source rules, coordinate/price checks, search and map indexes, and RLS.

nodes.name: 20261113000003_participation_reliability.sql
nodes.summary: Migration 3: creates event_participants (join status and QR token) and reliability_log (points history), with RLS.

nodes.name: 20261113000004_places.sql
nodes.summary: Migration 4: creates the places table for OpenStreetMap imports, unique by osm_id, with category and location indexes and RLS.

nodes.name: .mcp.json
nodes.summary: Claude Code MCP configuration registering the hosted Supabase MCP server over HTTP, scoped to this project's Supabase ref with database, docs, debugging and branching features enabled.

nodes.name: AGENTS.md
nodes.summary: Contributor and agent rules for the hackathon project: the Connected Communities problem statement, team rules (update DOCS.md, keep the knowledge graph current, write tests, comment functions), the core feature list and the Spring Boot + Supabase + Expo tech stack with its package layout convention.

nodes.name: DOCS.md
nodes.summary: Main project documentation covering architecture, backend configuration and running instructions, the shared backend foundation classes, Supabase MCP setup, database tables, external data sources (STPT, LiveTickets, OpenStreetMap, Gemini), reliability point rules and knowledge-graph maintenance.

nodes.name: PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Project plan and task list split into three tracks (backend, data/AI services, mobile), with 17 numbered steps from foundation, database and security through events, QR check-in, places, transit, routing, AI and frontend pages, plus a dependency map, cut order and open questions.

nodes.summary: Placeholder repository README containing only the project title; real documentation lives in DOCS.md and PLAN.md.

nodes.name: findJavaFromJavaHome
nodes.summary: Batch label that resolves java.exe from the JAVA_HOME environment variable and reports an error if JAVA_HOME points to an invalid directory.

nodes.name: execute
nodes.summary: Batch label that sets up the classpath to the gradle-wrapper jar and launches the Gradle Wrapper main class with the collected JVM options and command-line arguments.

nodes.name: settings.gradle
nodes.summary: Gradle settings file that names the root project 'backend' for the single-module Spring Boot build.

nodes.summary: Java record holding items, page, size, totalItems and totalPages; static of() maps a Spring Data Page through an entity-to-DTO mapper.

nodes.name: BackendApplicationTests.java
nodes.summary: Spring Boot smoke test verifying the application context loads with the test configuration.

nodes.name: BackendApplicationTests
nodes.summary: @SpringBootTest class with a contextLoads test.

nodes.name: SupabasePropertiesTest.java
nodes.summary: Unit tests checking that SupabaseProperties.issuer() appends /auth/v1 and ignores trailing slashes in the URL.

nodes.summary: JUnit test class with issuerAppendsAuthPath and issuerIgnoresTrailingSlash cases.

nodes.name: UserController.java
nodes.summary: REST controller for /users (PLAN 4): the public GET /users/username-available check plus the authenticated GET /users/me, PATCH /users/me, GET /users/search and GET /users/{id}, all delegating to UserService and reading the caller id from CurrentUser.

nodes.name: UserController
nodes.summary: @RestController under /users with five endpoints; business rules and errors live in UserService and the shared exception handler.

nodes.name: usernameAvailable
nodes.summary: Public GET /users/username-available: returns whether a username is free so the sign-up screen can check it before creating the account.

nodes.name: me
nodes.summary: GET /users/me: returns the caller's profile using the user id from the verified token.

nodes.name: updateMe
nodes.summary: PATCH /users/me: changes the caller's username and returns the updated profile.

nodes.name: search
nodes.summary: GET /users/search?q=: username-prefix search, at most 20 results.

nodes.name: byId
nodes.summary: GET /users/{id}: another user's public profile with attended events.

nodes.name: UserService.java
nodes.summary: Service contract for users: get a profile with attended events, change a username, search usernames by prefix and check whether a username is free.

nodes.name: UserService
nodes.summary: Interface with getProfile, updateUsername, search and checkUsername; failures are ApiException codes (NOT_FOUND, INVALID_USERNAME, USERNAME_TAKEN, VALIDATION_FAILED).

nodes.name: UserServiceImpl.java
nodes.summary: Implements the users rules: validates usernames (3-20 letters, digits or underscore), rejects case-insensitive duplicates including database races, caps prefix search at 20 results and assembles profiles with their attended events.
nodes.languageNotes: Catches DataIntegrityViolationException from saveAndFlush to turn a database uniqueness race into the same USERNAME_TAKEN answer as the precheck.

nodes.name: UserServiceImpl
nodes.summary: @Service that throws ApiException with ErrorCode values instead of feature-specific exceptions, so the global handler produces the standard error JSON.

nodes.name: getProfile
nodes.summary: Loads a profile or throws NOT_FOUND, then attaches the user's attended events through the mapper.

nodes.name: updateUsername
nodes.summary: Validates the format, rejects a name owned by another user and turns a concurrent database uniqueness violation into USERNAME_TAKEN.

nodes.name: search
nodes.summary: Trims the query, rejects an empty one with VALIDATION_FAILED and returns up to 20 profiles ordered by username.

nodes.name: checkUsername
nodes.summary: Validates the format and reports whether nobody owns the username yet, ignoring case.

nodes.name: requireValidUsername
nodes.summary: Throws 400 INVALID_USERNAME unless the name is 3-20 letters, digits or underscores (same rule as the profiles table check).

nodes.name: ProfileRepository.java
nodes.summary: Spring Data JPA repository for profiles with derived queries: case-insensitive duplicate checks (with and without the current user excluded) and capped username-prefix search.

nodes.name: ProfileRepository
nodes.summary: JpaRepository<Profile, UUID> adding existsByUsernameIgnoreCaseAndIdNot, existsByUsernameIgnoreCase and findByUsernameStartingWithIgnoreCase.

nodes.name: AttendedEventRepository.java
nodes.summary: Read-only contract that lists the events a user really attended, returned in the EventSummary shape.

nodes.languageNotes: Uses plain SQL so the users track does not duplicate JPA entities the events track will own.

nodes.name: AttendedEventRepositoryImpl
nodes.summary: @Repository running one SQL query against the Supabase events tables without declaring entities for them.

nodes.name: findAttendedByUserId
nodes.summary: Runs the attended-events SQL and maps each row to AttendedEventResponse, converting nullable columns and timestamps.

nodes.name: Profile.java
nodes.summary: JPA entity for the profiles table (id, username, reliability_score, created_at); rows are created by the Supabase sign-up trigger, so the only mutation is changeUsername.

nodes.name: Profile
nodes.summary: @Entity mapped to public.profiles with a protected JPA constructor and a public constructor for tests.

nodes.name: ProfileMapper.java
nodes.summary: Mapper contract that turns a Profile and its attended events into the profile response, and a Profile into the compact search result.

nodes.name: ProfileMapper
nodes.summary: Interface with toResponse and toSearchResult.

nodes.name: ProfileMapperImpl.java
nodes.summary: Hand-written mapper copying entity fields into ProfileResponse and ProfileSearchResult.

nodes.name: ProfileMapperImpl
nodes.summary: @Component implementing ProfileMapper without a mapping library.

nodes.name: ProfileResponse.java
nodes.summary: Profile answer of GET /users/me and /users/{id}: id, username, reliabilityScore, createdAt and the attended events.

nodes.name: ProfileResponse
nodes.summary: Java record matching the user profile shape in docs/API.md.

nodes.name: ProfileSearchResult.java

nodes.name: ProfileSearchResult

nodes.name: UpdateUsernameRequest

nodes.name: UsernameAvailabilityResponse.java

nodes.name: UsernameAvailabilityResponse

layers.name: Project Documentation

layers.name: API Contract

layers.name: Backend Shared Web Layer
layers.description: Cross-cutting common/dto and common/exception types (paging params and responses, ErrorResponse, ApiException, ErrorCode, GlobalExceptionHandler) that every feature controller will reuse.

layers.name: Backend Tests
layers.description: JUnit tests for the backend context, the users feature (controller, service, repositories), security filter chain, Supabase properties, paging and error handling, plus the support package (JWT test token minting, probe controller) and test properties.

layers.name: Backend Build & Config
layers.description: Gradle build scripts and wrapper plus Spring application properties (including the local Supabase secrets template) that build and configure the backend.

layers.name: Database Schema
layers.description: Supabase Postgres migrations defining profiles, events, participation/reliability tracking, and places tables, plus SQL schema checks verifying them.

layers.name: Infrastructure & Tooling
layers.description: OpenTripPlanner setup for STPT transit routing and the Supabase MCP server configuration used by development tooling.

layers.name: Frontend App
layers.description: Expo Router screens (root layout and home) and src/lib helpers for calling the backend API and map logic, with their Node test.

layers.name: Frontend Config
layers.description: Expo app manifest, npm package and scripts, path aliases, ESLint rules, and the environment template pointing the mobile client at the backend.

layers.name: Backend Users & Profiles
layers.description: The first backend feature (PLAN 4): the /users controller, service, JPA profile entity, repositories (including the JDBC attended-events query), mapper and DTOs. It builds on the shared common.* error, security and paging pieces.

tour.title: Project Vision and Plan
tour.description: The README is only a title, so the real starting point is AGENTS.md, which states the Connected Communities problem, the team rules (tests for every change, keep DOCS.md and the knowledge graph current) and the core idea: a Timișoara map with places, live STPT transit, directions, an AI guide and community events with reliability points. PLAN.md turns that vision into numbered tasks split across backend, data/AI services and mobile tracks, so you can see what exists now and what comes next.

tour.title: Living Documentation Hub
tour.description: DOCS.md is the most connected document in the project: it covers architecture, backend configuration and run instructions, and the shared backend foundation you will meet later in this tour. Because the rules require updating it with every change, treat it as the current map of the system and come back to it whenever a later step feels unfamiliar.

tour.title: Users and Profiles Schema
tour.description: The data model starts in Supabase Postgres. Migration 1 enables pg_trgm and creates public.profiles, one row per Supabase auth user with a case-insensitive unique username, filled automatically by the on_auth_user_created trigger. Profiles are the most referenced table, because events, participation and reliability all point back to a user.
tour.languageLesson: A Postgres trigger on auth.users lets the database create the app-side profile row the moment someone signs up, so the backend never has to remember to do it.

tour.title: Events on the Map
tour.description: Building on profiles, migration 2 creates public.events for both user-created (USER) and imported (EXTERNAL) events. Check constraints enforce source rules, valid coordinates and prices at the database level, so bad data cannot reach the map no matter which client writes it.

tour.title: Participation and Reliability
tour.description: This migration models the project's signature feature. event_participants joins users to events with a status lifecycle (JOINED, ATTENDED, NO_SHOW, CANCELLED) and the QR token used for check-in, while reliability_log records every signed point change as an audit trail. Together they make reliability points explainable rather than a single opaque counter.
tour.languageLesson: An append-only log table like reliability_log is a common SQL pattern: each change is stored as a row and totals are derived from it, so history is never lost.

tour.title: Places from OpenStreetMap
tour.description: Migration 4 adds public.places for restaurants, cafes and other points of interest imported from OpenStreetMap, kept unique by osm_id so re-imports update rows instead of duplicating them. These rows power the category filters on the map and will feed the AI guide.

tour.title: Verifying the Schema
tour.description: schema_checks.sql is a self-rolling-back PL/pgSQL block that tests the rules from the previous four steps: profile creation on sign-up, username formats and the table constraints. It leaves no data behind, so it can be run safely against the shared Supabase database.

tour.title: The REST API Contract
tour.description: docs/API.md defines how the mobile app talks to the backend: conventions, the paged and error answer shapes, shared objects and the planned endpoints. The next backend steps implement exactly these shapes, so reading the contract first makes the Java code easy to follow.

tour.title: Spring Boot Entry and Settings
tour.description: BackendApplication bootstraps the Spring Boot API, and its smoke test checks that the context loads. SupabaseProperties binds the Supabase URL and legacy HS256 JWT secret and derives the token issuer, TimeConfig exposes a shared UTC Clock so time logic can be tested, and application.properties tells Hibernate to only validate against the Supabase migrations instead of creating tables.
tour.languageLesson: Java records annotated with @ConfigurationProperties give immutable, validated config objects, and injecting a Clock bean instead of calling Instant.now() lets tests freeze time.

tour.title: Security and the Current User
tour.description: SecurityConfig makes the backend a stateless JWT resource server: Supabase access tokens are validated with the secret and issuer from the previous step, public GET routes for events and places stay open, and everything else requires a token. CurrentUser then reads the token's sub claim to give services the caller's UUID, and the JSON entry point and access-denied handler make 401 and 403 answers use the same error format as the rest of the API.
tour.languageLesson: In modern Spring Security you declare a SecurityFilterChain bean; configuring oauth2ResourceServer with a JWT decoder means every request is authenticated before any controller runs.

tour.title: One Error Format Everywhere
tour.description: ErrorCode is the most depended-on file in the backend: an enum listing every API error, from validation and auth to QR check-in and rate limiting. Code throws ApiException with a code, GlobalExceptionHandler catches it (plus validation and malformed-body errors), and ErrorResponseFactory builds the ErrorResponse record, the single error JSON shape promised in docs/API.md and shared with the security handlers from Step 10.
tour.languageLesson: @RestControllerAdvice with @ExceptionHandler methods centralises error handling, so controllers just throw and never build error bodies themselves.

tour.title: Paging Lists
tour.description: PageParams is an immutable record that enforces the API paging rules (page starts at 0, default size 20, capped at 100 for lists) and rejects bad input through the error system from the previous step. PageResponse is the matching generic answer shape from docs/API.md, with a factory that converts Spring Data pages so every future list endpoint looks the same.
tour.languageLesson: Java records can validate their fields in a compact constructor, and a generic record like PageResponse<T> gives one reusable, type-safe wrapper for any list.

tour.title: The Users and Profiles Feature
tour.description: The first feature built on the foundation. UserController exposes GET /users/username-available (public) and GET/PATCH /users/me, /users/search and /users/{id} (token required). UserServiceImpl holds the rules: usernames are 3-20 letters, digits or underscores, case-insensitive duplicates answer USERNAME_TAKEN even when two requests race, and search stops at 20 results. Errors are plain ApiException codes, so the shared handler produces the standard error JSON. Profiles come from the Supabase profiles table through JPA, while attended events come from a JDBC query over events and event_participants that returns the EventSummary shape.
tour.languageLesson: Keeping the attended-events query as plain JDBC means the users feature needs no JPA entity for tables another feature owns, so the two features can change independently.

tour.title: Backend Tests with Real JWTs
tour.description: The foundation is covered by tests that run on an in-memory H2 database in PostgreSQL mode with a fake Supabase secret. JwtTestTokens signs HS256 tokens shaped like real Supabase access tokens, and TestProbeController (test-only, never shipped) exposes probe endpoints so SecurityConfigTest and GlobalExceptionHandlerTest can hit public and protected routes with MockMvc and check the exact error JSON.

tour.title: Backend Build and Tooling
tour.description: build.gradle targets Java 21 and Spring Boot with JPA, Security and Validation, while the Gradle wrapper pins a fixed Gradle version so every teammate builds the same way. The application-local properties example lists the Supabase URL, JWT secret and pooler connection each developer fills into a git-ignored local profile.
tour.languageLesson: The Gradle wrapper (gradlew plus gradle-wrapper.properties) downloads the pinned Gradle version on first run, so nobody needs Gradle installed globally.

tour.title: Expo App Shell and Discover
tour.description: Switching to the mobile app, _layout.jsx is the Expo Router root that sets up the status bar and native Stack navigator, and index.jsx is the Discover home screen rendering a react-native-maps MapView centered on Timișoara. map.js supplies the frozen TIMISOARA_CENTER coordinates and a validated region builder, keeping map math out of the UI.
tour.languageLesson: Expo Router uses file-based routing: _layout.jsx wraps every screen in its folder, and index.jsx becomes the default route.

tour.title: Talking to the Backend
tour.description: api.js is the app's minimal HTTP client: it resolves the backend base URL from EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL, defined in .env.example as the LAN address of the Spring Boot server, and wraps GET requests. setup.test.mjs uses node:test to check both the URL handling here and the coordinate validation in map.js.
tour.languageLesson: Expo only exposes environment variables prefixed with EXPO_PUBLIC_ to app code, and they are inlined at build time, so never put secrets in them.

tour.title: Frontend Configuration
tour.description: package.json pins Expo SDK 54, React Native 0.81, expo-router, expo-location and react-native-maps, and app.json is the Expo manifest naming the app 'Connected Communities' with its deep-link scheme and icons. jsconfig.json turns on type checking for plain JS files, and frontend/AGENTS.md reminds contributors to follow versioned Expo docs and use expo install.

tour.title: Transit Routing and Dev Tooling
tour.description: infra/otp/README.md describes the planned OpenTripPlanner 2 server on port 8081, called only by the backend, that will compute walking and public transport directions for Timișoara. .mcp.json registers the hosted Supabase MCP server for this project, which is how AI tooling inspects and migrates the database you studied earlier.
